content.text: Now the M1 page: the state machine, every ABDM call, and Care's facade contract. I'll add the UI section once the frontend exists.

content.input:
{"content": "# M1: ABHA at the desk

M1 lets a desk find or create a patient's ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health
Account), read the verified profile, fill the registration form from it, and
link it to the patient record.

Sources: `.github/skills/abdm-m1/` (`SKILL.md`, `references/design.md`,
`references/scaffold.md`, `references/integrate.md`) and
https://docs.abdm.gov.in/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m1.md.

## Rules that are not negotiable

These come from the skill's `design.md`. Each one was a production defect
before it became a rule.

1. **Look before you create.** Every identifier, Aadhaar included, goes to a
   lookup first. Only `ABDM-1114` means nobody holds an ABHA. Nothing merges
   duplicate ABHAs, so a duplicate is permanent.
2. **Create only from Aadhaar.** If the mobile lookup finds no ABHA, ask for
   the Aadhaar number, and look that up too.
3. **The journey finishes without an ABHA.** Every screen has a "not now"
   exit that returns to the registration form.
4. **Never ask twice.** Facts collected in an earlier step, such as the
   mobile number or the Aadhaar ciphertext, carry forward in the flow.
5. **Branch on `refreshToken`, not on `accounts.length`.** If the verify
   response has a `refreshToken`, its `token` is already the user token, so
   do not call `verify/user`. If it has none, `token` is a short-lived
   T-token that must be exchanged at `verify/user`.
6. **Fill the form, do not save it unseen.** The profile pre-fills the form,
   and the desk confirms it. A correction changes the hospital's record, not
   ABDM's.
7. **Tell the truth on screen.** Show errors on the step that is in view. A
   refusal must never look like a success. Show the masked number the OTP
   was sent to.

## State machine (what Care's facade returns)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Identify
    Identify --> OtpSent: aadhaar / abha_number found
    Identify --> AccountsFound: mobile lookup found accounts (no OTP yet)
    Identify --> NotFound: ABDM-1114
    AccountsFound --> OtpSent: desk picks an account (search-account)
    OtpSent --> Authenticated: verify-otp, refreshToken present
    OtpSent --> Authenticated: verify-otp, 1 account (auto exchange)
    OtpSent --> SelectAccount: verify-otp, 2+ accounts
    SelectAccount --> Authenticated: select-account
    NotFound --> Identify: mobile -> ask for Aadhaar (lookup again)
    NotFound --> EnrolOtpSent: aadhaar -> enrol/request-otp (reuses ciphertext)
    EnrolOtpSent --> Authenticated: enrol/verify-otp
    Authenticated --> MobileOtp: mobile_verification_required
    MobileOtp --> Authenticated: enrol/mobile/verify-otp
    Authenticated --> AddressChosen: enrol/address (optional)
    Authenticated --> Linked: link (patient exists)
    Authenticated --> FormFilled: registration form, then link after save
    Linked --> [*]
    FormFilled --> [*]
```

## Care's facade API (`/api/v1/abdm/abha/`)

All endpoints are `POST` with a JSON body unless marked otherwise. Every
response carries `status` and `flow_id`. Errors use the shape
`{"errors": [{"type": "abdm_error", "code", "msg", "fields", "request_id"}]}`,
with status 400 for a refusal and 502 when ABDM is unavailable or refused
Care's own credentials.

| Endpoint | Body | Returns `status` | ABDM calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET config/` | none | `{enabled, demographic_auth_enabled}` | none |
| `identify/` | `{identifier_type: aadhaar\|mobile\|abha_number, value, otp_system?: aadhaar\|abdm, flow_id?}` | `otp_sent` / `accounts_found` / `not_found` | aadhaar, abha_number: `POST /v3/profile/login/request/otp`. mobile: `POST /v3/profile/account/abha/search` |
| `search-account/` | `{flow_id, index}` | `otp_sent` | `POST /v3/profile/login/request/otp` with `loginHint: index` |
| `verify-otp/` | `{flow_id, otp}` | `authenticated` / `select_account` | `POST /v3/profile/login/verify`, then (if no refreshToken) `/verify/user`, then `GET /v3/profile/account` |
| `select-account/` | `{flow_id, abha_number}` | `authenticated` | `POST /v3/profile/login/verify/user` (T-token), `GET /v3/profile/account` |
| `enrol/request-otp/` | `{flow_id, resend?}` | `otp_sent` | `POST /v3/enrollment/request/otp` |
| `enrol/verify-otp/` | `{flow_id, otp, mobile?}` | `authenticated` + `is_new`, `mobile_verification_required` | `POST /v3/enrollment/enrol/byAadhaar` |
| `enrol/mobile/request-otp/` | `{flow_id, mobile}` | `otp_sent` | `POST /v3/enrollment/request/otp` (`mobile-verify`) |
| `enrol/mobile/verify-otp/` | `{flow_id, otp}` | `authenticated` | `POST /v3/enrollment/auth/byAbdm` |
| `enrol/address-suggestions/` | `{flow_id}` | `{suggestions: [...]}` | `GET /v3/enrollment/enrol/suggestion` (`TRANSACTION_ID` header) |
| `enrol/address/` | `{flow_id, abha_address}` | `authenticated` | `POST /v3/enrollment/enrol/abha-address` |
| `enrol/demographic/` | `{aadhaar, name, date_of_birth (dd-MM-yyyy), gender (M/F/O), state_code, district_code, mobile?, pincode?, address?}` | `authenticated` | `POST /v3/enrollment/enrol/byAadhaar` (`demo_auth`, `BENEFIT_NAME` header). Off unless `ABDM_DEMOGRAPHIC_AUTH_ENABLED` |
| `profile/` | `{flow_id}` | `authenticated` | `GET /v3/profile/account` |
| `GET card/?flow_id=` | none | image bytes | `GET /v3/profile/account/abha-card` |
| `GET qr-code/?flow_id=` | none | image bytes | `GET /v3/profile/account/qrCode` |
| `mobile/request-otp/` | `{flow_id, mobile}` | `otp_sent` | `POST /v3/profile/account/request/otp` (X-token) |
| `mobile/verify-otp/` | `{flow_id, otp}` | `authenticated` | `POST /v3/profile/account/verify` (X-token) |
| `link/` | `{flow_id, patient}` | the `AbhaNumber` record | none (DB only) |
| `GET patient/?patient=` | none | the `AbhaNumber` linked to the patient, or 404 | none |

The `authenticated` response carries `profile`, which is the normalised
profile:

```json
{
  "abha_number": "91-1111-2222-3333", "abha_address": "jane@sbx", "abha_addresses": ["jane@sbx"],
  "name": "Jane Doe", "first_name": "Jane", "middle_name": null, "last_name": "Doe",
  "gender": "F", "care_gender": "female", "date_of_birth": "1990-04-09", "year_of_birth": 1990,
  "mobile": "******3210", "email": null, "address": "...", "pincode": "560001",
  "state_code": "29", "state_name": "KARNATAKA", "district_code": "...", "district_name": "...",
  "kyc_verified": true, "status": "ACTIVE", "photo": "<base64 or null>"
}
```

It also carries `linked_patient`. If this ABHA is already linked to a Care
patient, that is `{id, name}`, or `{id: null, name: null}` when the user
cannot see that patient. Otherwise it is `null`. Use it to open the existing
record instead of registering a second patient.

## The ABDM calls, with what each needs

Every call sends `Authorization: Bearer <gateway token>`, `REQUEST-ID` and
`TIMESTAMP`. Scopes must be sent exactly as listed.

| Job | Path | scope | loginHint / otpSystem | Encrypted fields | Extra headers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Login lookup by Aadhaar | `POST /v3/profile/login/request/otp` | `abha-login, aadhaar-verify` | `aadhaar` / `aadhaar` | loginId | |
| Login lookup by ABHA number, Aadhaar OTP | same | `abha-login, aadhaar-verify` | `abha-number` / `aadhaar` | loginId (**with dashes**) | |
| Login lookup by ABHA number, mobile OTP | same | `abha-login, mobile-verify` | `abha-number` / `abdm` | loginId (**with dashes**) | |
| Find ABHA by mobile (free) | `POST /v3/profile/account/abha/search` | `search-abha` | n/a | mobile | |
| Send OTP to the found account | `POST /v3/profile/login/request/otp` | `abha-login, search-abha, mobile-verify` | `index` / `abdm`, plus `txnId` from the search | loginId (= the index as a string) | |
| Verify login OTP | `POST /v3/profile/login/verify` | the request's scope, minus `search-abha` | n/a | otpValue | |
| Exchange T-token | `POST /v3/profile/login/verify/user` | n/a | n/a | none | `T-token: Bearer <token>` |
| Enrolment OTP | `POST /v3/enrollment/request/otp` | `abha-enrol` | `aadhaar` / `aadhaar` | loginId | |
| Create by Aadhaar OTP | `POST /v3/enrollment/enrol/byAadhaar` | n/a; `authMethods: [otp]`; `consent: {code: abha-enrollment, version: 1.4}` | n/a | otpValue (mobile is **plain**) | |
| Profile | `GET /v3/profile/account` | n/a | n/a | n/a | `X-token: Bearer <token>` |

The full request bodies are in `care/abdm/service/abha.py`. That file is
the most compact correct reference, so copy its shapes rather than the
examples in the portal, which carry placeholders.

## Response shapes to expect (plural where ABDM is plural)

- **Search by mobile** returns an **array**. Each element has a `txnId` and an
  `ABHA` array of `{index, ABHANumber (masked), name, gender, kycVerified, authMethods}`.
  Flatten it, and keep each account's `txnId`.
- **Login verify** returns `accounts` (an array), `token`, and `refreshToken`
  only when the token is final.
- **Create by Aadhaar** returns `ABHAProfile`, `tokens.token`, and `isNew`.
  `isNew: false` with the message "This account already exist" means the
  Aadhaar already had an ABHA. ABDM returns that ABHA, so no duplicate is made.
- **Create by demographics** returns a different shape: `healthIdNumber`,
  `healthId`, `jwtResponse.token`, `new`.
- The **profile mobile is masked** (`******3210`). Do not copy it into a phone
  field.

## Mapping the profile onto a patient form

| Profile | Care form field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name` | Show as "from ABHA". The desk may correct transliteration |
| `care_gender` | `gender` | `M` maps to male and `F` to female. Leave `O` blank: Care's options (non_binary, transgender) are more specific than ABDM's |
| `date_of_birth` / `year_of_birth` | `date_of_birth` or age | Use the year only if the full date is missing |
| `mobile` | `phone_number` | Only if it is unmasked. Otherwise keep the mobile the desk typed |
| `address` | `address` | |
| `pincode` | `pincode` | |
| `state_name` / `district_name` | geo organisation | Not auto-mapped: Care's organisation tree does not carry LGD codes. Shown as a hint |
| `abha_number`, `abha_address` | not a form field | Linked after the patient is saved, through `link/` |

{"content": "# ABDM integration: findings

Hiccups, gaps in the official sources, and decisions taken where the sources
were silent. Newest entries go at the end of each section.

Sources used: the ABDM skills in `.github/skills/abdm-*` (catalogue
2026.09.16), the ABDM Developer Portal (https://docs.abdm.gov.in/, including
its M1 Postman collection and per-endpoint `.md` pages), and the sandbox
itself. Nothing else was used.

## About `~/ohc.network/care-abdm-sbx`

- The earlier plugin attempt was **not read**. The guard rails allow only the
  skills, the MCP server and the docs they point to, so no design was taken
  from it.
- One indirect influence: the environment variable **names** already in
  Care's `.env` (`ABDM_CLIENT_ID`, `ABDM_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ABDM_GATEWAY_URL`,
  `ABDM_ABHA_URL`, `ABDM_CM_ID`, `ABDM_CALLBACK_BASE_URL`,
  `ABDM_DEVELOPER_MODE`) were probably set up for that attempt. Care reuses
  the first five names so that existing environments keep working.
  `ABDM_ABHA_URL` already included `/abha/api`, so Care appends
  `/v3/...` to it. `ABDM_DEVELOPER_MODE` is not used, because no source
  defines its meaning. `ABDM_CALLBACK_BASE_URL` is left for M2.

## Tooling hiccups

1. **The `abdm-docs` MCP server was not reachable from this session.** It was
   registered in VS Code but did not load as a tool. The portal was read
   through its `.md` page variants and the Postman collection instead.
2. **The M1 Postman collection has no example responses.** Response shapes
   came from the per-endpoint pages
   (`/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m1/endpoints/<journey>/<nn>-<operation>.md`), which do
   carry them.
3. **One gateway session call failed intermittently.** One call in a quick
   burst got no `accessToken`, and the retry succeeded. The body was not
   captured, which was a mistake. The transport now logs every refusal body
   with its REQUEST-ID.

## Contradictions and gaps in the official sources

1. **Benefit header name.** The skill's curl uses `BENEFIT_NAME`, while the
   portal's header table says `Benefit-Name`. Care sends `BENEFIT_NAME`, as
   the curl does. Note that nginx drops headers containing underscores by
   default. Unverified, because it needs an NHA-approved client.
2. **ABHA number format for `loginId`.** The spec says only "RSA-encrypted".
   The sandbox refuses an undashed 14 digit number with `LoginId is invalid`
   and accepts the dashed form. The skill's design page does mention this.
   Care adds the dashes when the desk types 14 bare digits.
3. **The `ABHAProfile.dob` format on create is undocumented.** Care parses
   `dd-MM-yyyy`, which matches the demographic input format, falls back to
   `yyyy-MM-dd`, and leaves the field empty otherwise. Unverified.
4. **Mobile "is it already linked?" after create.** The spec says to verify
   the mobile only if it is not the Aadhaar-linked one, but the response only
   carries a masked mobile. Care compares the last four digits. That is a
   heuristic, not a documented rule.
5. **Resending a login OTP.** Enrolment documents resending with the previous
   `txnId`. Login does not. Care's resend for login starts a new lookup.
6. **The search-by-mobile response is an array of results**, each with its
   own `txnId` and `ABHA` array. The relationship between multiple results is
   undocumented. Care flattens them and keeps each account's own `txnId`.
7. **The demographic response shape differs from the OTP create response.**
   It has `healthIdNumber`/`healthId`/`jwtResponse` rather than
   `ABHAProfile`/`tokens`. The normaliser handles both.
8. **The skill's advice to put "ABHA number and address as columns beside the
   existing identifiers"** does not fit Care. Care's identifiers are
   configured per deployment, and M1 to M4 need more state than one value.
   Care uses an `AbhaNumber` table, one-to-one with `Patient`. See
   `docs/abdm/architecture.md`.

## Decisions taken where the sources were silent

1. **No ABDM user tokens are persisted.** The `X-token` and refresh token live
   only in the 30 minute server-side flow. Showing the card or updating the
   mobile later means verifying again with an OTP. This favours consent and a
   smaller blast radius over convenience. If that is too costly at the desk,
   store the refresh token encrypted at rest. That is a deliberate change,
   not a default.
2. **Mobile identifier uses "search" (free lookup) before any OTP**, rather
   than "Login via mobile number". The search reveals how many accounts the
   handset carries before an OTP is spent, and it serves both "login" and
   "find a forgotten ABHA".
3. **ABDM 401 and 5xx map to HTTP 502** in Care's API. Care's frontend treats
   401 as its own session expiring.
4. **The flow store keeps the Aadhaar ciphertext, never the plaintext**, so
   creation after a not-found lookup does not ask for the Aadhaar again.
5. **Linking is separate from registration.** The form fills from the
   profile, the patient is saved through Care's normal patient API, and the
   ABHA is linked afterwards with the same flow. The ABHA is never required
   to save a patient.
6. **`cryptography` is used transitively** (it comes with `authlib`) and is
   not pinned directly in the `Pipfile`, to avoid re-locking in this change.
   Pin it when the lockfile is next refreshed.
7. **No rate limiting on OTP endpoints yet.** They need `can_create_patient`,
   which limits exposure. Per-user throttling should be added before
   production.
8. **The ABHA is not mirrored into `PatientIdentifier`.** A deployment that
   wants ABHA searchable through Care's identifier search can add a config.
   Automatic mirroring is a follow-up.
9. **State and district are not auto-mapped** to Care's geo organisations.
   ABDM sends LGD codes and names, and Care's organisation tree has no LGD
   codes.
", "filePath": "/Users/rithviknishad/ohc.network/care/findings.md"}

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from drf_spectacular.utils import extend_schema
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.viewsets import GenericViewSet

from care.emr.api.viewsets.base import emr_exception_handler
from care.emr.utils.batch_requests import execute_batch_requests


class Request(BaseModel):
    url: str
    method: str
    body: dict = {}
    reference_id: str


class BatchRequest(BaseModel):
    requests: list[Request] = Field(
        ..., min_length=1, max_length=settings.MAX_REQUESTS_PER_BATCH_REQUEST
    )


class HandledError(Exception):
    pass


class UnHandledError(Exception):
    pass


class BatchRequestView(GenericViewSet):
    def get_exception_handler(self):
        return emr_exception_handler

    @extend_schema(
        request=BatchRequest,
    )
    def create(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        requests = BatchRequest(**request.data)
        errored = False
        loop = 0
        try:
            with transaction.atomic():
                responses = execute_batch_requests(request, requests)
                structured_responses = []
                for response in responses:
                    if response["status_code"] > 299:  # noqa PLR2004
                        errored = True
                    if response["status_code"] >= 500:  # noqa PLR2004
                        structured_responses.append(
                            {
                                "reference_id": requests.requests[loop].reference_id,
                                "status_code": response["status_code"],
                            }
                        )
                        raise UnHandledError
                    structured_responses.append(
                        {
                            "reference_id": requests.requests[loop].reference_id,
                            "data": response["data"],
                            "status_code": response["status_code"],
                        }
                    )
                    loop += 1
                if errored:
                    raise HandledError
        except HandledError:
            return Response({"results": structured_responses}, status=400)
        except UnHandledError:
            return Response({"results": structured_responses}, status=500)
        return Response({"results": structured_responses})

) {

import careConfig from "@careConfig";

import {
  ApiCallOptions,
  ApiRoute,
  HTTPError,
  PaginatedResponse,
} from "@/Utils/request/types";
import { getResponseBody, makeHeaders, makeUrl } from "@/Utils/request/utils";
import { sleep } from "@/Utils/utils";

export async function callApi<Route extends ApiRoute<unknown, unknown>>(
  { baseUrl, path, method, noAuth, defaultQueryParams }: Route,
  options?: ApiCallOptions<Route>,
): Promise<Route["TRes"]> {
  const url = `${baseUrl ?? careConfig.apiUrl}${makeUrl(
    path,
    {
      ...(defaultQueryParams ?? {}),
      ...options?.queryParams,
    },
    options?.pathParams,
  )}`;

  const isFormData = options?.body instanceof FormData;

  const fetchOptions: RequestInit = {
    method,
    headers: makeHeaders(noAuth ?? false, options?.headers, isFormData),
    signal: options?.signal,
  };

  if (options?.body) {
    if (isFormData) {
      fetchOptions.body = options.body as FormData;
    } else {
      fetchOptions.body = JSON.stringify(options.body);
    }
  }

  let res: Response;

  try {
    res = await fetch(url, fetchOptions);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error("Network Error", { cause: error });
  }

  const data = await getResponseBody<Route["TRes"]>(res);

  if (!res.ok) {
    const isSilent =
      typeof options?.silent === "function"
        ? options.silent(res)
        : (options?.silent ?? false);

    throw new HTTPError({
      message: "Request Failed",
      status: res.status,
      silent: isSilent,
      cause: data as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
    });
  }

  return data;
}

/**
 * Creates a TanStack Query compatible query function.
 *
 * Example:
 * ```tsx
 * const { data, isLoading } = useQuery({
 *   queryKey: ["prescription", consultationId],
 *   queryFn: query(MedicineRoutes.prescription, {
 *     pathParams: { consultationId },
 *     queryParams: {
 *       limit: 10,
 *       offset: 0,
 *     },
 *   }),
 * });
 * ```
 */
export default function query<Route extends ApiRoute<unknown, unknown>>(
  route: Route,
  options?: ApiCallOptions<Route>,
) {
  return ({ signal }: { signal: AbortSignal }) => {
    return callApi(route, { ...options, signal });
  };
}

/**
 * Creates a debounced TanStack Query compatible query function.
 *
 * Example:
 * ```tsx
 * const { data, isLoading } = useQuery({
 *   queryKey: ["patient-search", facilityId, search],
 *   queryFn: query.debounced(patientsApi.search, {
 *     pathParams: { facilityId },
 *     queryParams: { limit: 10, offset: 0, search },
 *   }),
 * });
 * ```
 *
 * The debounced query leverages TanStack Query's built-in cancellation through
 * `AbortSignal`. Here's how it works:
 *
 * 1. When a new query is triggered, TanStack Query automatically creates an
 * `AbortSignal`
 * 2. If a new query starts before the debounce delay finishes:
 *    - The previous signal is aborted automatically by TanStack Query
 *    - The previous `sleep` promise is cancelled
 *    - A new debounce timer starts
 *

 * - The `AbortSignal` is passed through to the underlying `fetch` call
 * - When aborted, both the `sleep` promise and the fetch request are cancelled automatically
 * - TanStack Query handles the abortion and cleanup of previous in-flight requests
 */
const debouncedQuery = <Route extends ApiRoute<unknown, unknown>>(
  route: Route,
  options?: ApiCallOptions<Route> & { debounceInterval?: number },
) => {
  return async ({ signal }: { signal: AbortSignal }) => {
    await sleep(options?.debounceInterval ?? 500);
    return query(route, { ...options })({ signal });
  };
};

## The desk UI (Care frontend)

All of it lives in `care_fe/src/components/Abdm/`. The API types are in
`care_fe/src/types/abdm/`. Strings are under the `abha_*` keys in
`care_fe/public/locale/en.json`.

| File | What it is | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| `AbhaVerifyDialog.tsx` | The whole journey as one dialog. It renders the screen that the backend's `status` names. All state lives inside the dialog content, so closing it wipes everything and nothing leaks into the next patient | Opened by the two placements below |
| `AbhaRegistrationPanel.tsx` | An "ABHA (optional)" card **above** the registration form. After verification it fills the form, shows which fields came from the ABHA, and remembers the `flow_id` | `PatientRegistration.tsx`, create mode only |
| `PatientAbhaSection.tsx` | Shows the linked ABHA, or a "Link ABHA" button | `PatientDetailsTab/Demography.tsx`, top of the page |
| `AbhaAccountDialog.tsx` | Card image, QR code, update mobile. Works only on a verified flow | Opened from either placement |
| `utils.ts` | `useAbdmConfig()` (feature switch from `GET config/`), `getAbdmError()`, `fetchAbhaImage()`, mobile and ABHA number helpers | |

### Screens, and what each must never ask

These are the six screens from `design.md`, mapped to Care's steps:

| Screen (design.md) | Care step | Collects | Never asks | Skipped when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identify | `identify` | one identifier (tabs: Aadhaar, Mobile, ABHA number). The OTP channel radio appears only for an ABHA number | anything the desk already holds. The form's phone pre-fills the mobile tab. The patient page locks the ABHA number | never |
| Confirm it is them | `accounts_found` | which listed account (masked) is theirs | the number itself | the identifier was not a mobile |
| One time password | `otp` | 6 digits. During creation, also the mobile to link, pre-filled from the lookup | the identifier again | n/a |
| Choose an account | `select_account` | which of several | anything in the `accounts` array | 1 account (auto-exchanged) or a `refreshToken` is present |
| Choose an address | `address` | pick a suggestion or type one | anything in the profile | the ABHA was not new |
| Confirm the form | `done`, then the registration form | corrections only | anything the profile carries | never |

Each screen has a **"Not now"** button, which closes the dialog and leaves the
form usable. Errors appear as an alert on the screen in view. They show the
message, the ABDM code and the REQUEST-ID (`ref …`). When ABDM names a field,
the alert says the cause is often the encryption, headers or clock, not the
patient's details.

### How registration links the ABHA

1. The desk opens the panel and verifies. `onProfile(profile)` fills
   `name`, `gender`, the date of birth (or age), `address` and `pincode`, plus
   `phone_number` only if it is unmasked. It returns the labels of the
   fields it filled.
2. The desk confirms and corrects the form, then submits through Care's
   normal `POST /api/v1/patient/`.
3. In `createPatient.onSuccess`, if the panel holds a session, Care calls
   `POST /api/v1/abdm/abha/link/ {flow_id, patient}`. A failure here does
   not undo the registration. The ABHA can be linked later from the patient
   page.

### Porting the UI to another system

The UI is a renderer of the facade's `status`. To port it:

- Build one dialog with a `switch` on `status`. Keep its state local, so it
  resets on close.
- Keep only `flow_id`, never tokens.
- Put the panel **before** the registration form. Make it optional, and let
  it fill fields rather than save them.
- Map `M`→male and `F`→female. Leave other genders for the desk to choose.
- Throttle "resend OTP" with a visible countdown. Care waits 60 seconds.

content.text:
M1 is built into Care directly (not as a plug), with docs written alongside so an agent can repeat it on another hospital system. The backend tests pass and the live sandbox calls behave correctly. But no journey has been run with a real OTP, and the screens haven't been opened in a browser.

**What's verified:**
- **Backend tests:** 23 pass, and the linter is clean.
- **Frontend:** type-check is clean.
- **Live sandbox, through Care's own API:** the session token, the encryption certificate, encryption, the "no ABHA found" lookup and field-level error messages all behaved correctly. I used ABHA numbers and a mobile number nobody holds, so no OTP was sent to anyone.
- **Not yet observed:** verify, create, card, QR and mobile update all need a sandbox test identity that can receive OTPs. Those response shapes come from the docs until someone runs them.

**Backend (`care/abdm/`):**
- A gateway token and the encryption certificate are cached until they expire. The encryption padding is read from what ABDM publishes, and an unrecognised one is refused.
- The API at `/api/v1/abdm/abha/` covers: find by Aadhaar, mobile or ABHA number; choosing between several accounts; create by Aadhaar OTP; create by demographics (only if `ABDM_DEMOGRAPHIC_AUTH_ENABLED` is set); mobile verification; ABHA address; profile, card and QR; mobile update; and linking to a patient.
- Every identifier is looked up before any ABHA can be created, so nobody ends up with two.
- ABDM's tokens never reach the browser and are never stored in the database. One consequence: showing the card later means the patient verifies again with an OTP.
- ABDM's 401 errors come back as 502, because the frontend reads a 401 as "your Care login expired" and logs the user out.
- The new `AbhaNumber` table links one ABHA to one patient; there's a migration for it.

**Frontend (`care_fe/src/components/Abdm/`):**
- **Registration page:** an optional ABHA card above the form. After verification it fills the form and shows which fields came from ABHA. The desk confirms before saving, and the ABHA is linked once the patient is saved. Registration still works without an ABHA.
- **Patient page:** shows the linked ABHA (replacing the old commented-out block), or a "Link ABHA" button. From there the desk can open the card, QR code and mobile update after re-verifying.
- 78 English strings were appended to `en.json`.
- ESLint flags only formatting (prettier) in the new files; I didn't run prettier, per the repo instructions.

**Docs (`care/docs/abdm/`):**
- `README.md`: the entry point and where each kind of fact should come from.
- `agent-playbook.md`: steps 0–8, each with an exit check, plus a table of mistakes cheaper models tend to make.
- `architecture.md`: the layers, what each guarantees, and where M2–M4 attach.
- `m1-abha.md`: the full flow, Care's API, the exact ABDM calls, the screens, and how to port the UI.
- `sandbox-observations.md`: what the sandbox actually returned, with request IDs.
- `integration-plan.md`: the survey of Care's codebase, as a template for other systems.

**`care/findings.md`** records every hiccup and decision. The ones to know about:
- I did **not** read `care-abdm-sbx`. The only carry-over is the existing `.env` variable names, which I reused so your environment keeps working.
- The `abdm-docs` MCP server didn't load in this session, so I read the portal pages directly instead.
- The docs contradict themselves on the benefit header name (`BENEFIT_NAME` vs `Benefit-Name`).
- The format of the date of birth returned on creation isn't documented.
- No source gives the official consent text to show the patient, so the checkbox wording is my own and should be replaced.
- There's no rate limiting on the OTP endpoints yet.
- Things I didn't build this session: fingerprint, iris and face routes (you said OTP only), and auto-mapping state/district to Care's location hierarchy.

I added a pointer to these docs in Care's `CLAUDE.md` and care_fe's `AGENTS.md`. I skipped the `AGENTS.md` instruction to star the GitHub repo, since it's an action on your account and not part of this task.

The `303001` "Runtime Error" was almost certainly a temporary ABDM outage, not a bug in Care. Care now shows it as "try again in a few minutes" instead of a failure. I couldn't confirm which call hit it: the backend log line didn't name the URL then, and your server runs in a terminal I can't read.
